label: copy-phase input c (early recall positions), sparse subset
explanation: Fires almost only during the copy phase (90% of mass) when the fed-back input token is c (81% of mass; lift 26x). Most of it falls at recall positions 1-4, peaking at 2-3. Precision is very low, though: only about 2-3% of copy-phase c inputs activate it, and adding conditions on out_tok (c or l are enriched about 14x), prev_tok, or next_out pushed precision to 20-30% at most while cutting recall below 35%. Smaller off-target pieces: copy-phase inputs b, 1, a (about 5% of mass each), and late original-phase steps (orig_idx 6-8, about 9% of mass). It is essentially silent at t<4, at the delimiter, and on most other tokens. Activations are weak (max 0.24) and fairly uniform; I found no reliable magnitude modulator beyond the higher rates at recall_idx 2-3 and when out_tok is c or l. Which c inputs fire seems to depend on sequence context that simple predicates do not capture.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=c (+4.33), in_tok=b (+4.00), in_tok=1 (+3.87), phase=0 & in_tok=p (+3.83), in_tok=a (+3.56), phase=2 & out_tok=l (+3.43). Lower it: prev3_tok=- (-2.59), prev_tok=x (-2.55), orig_idx=-1 (-2.47), prev_tok=l (-2.26).
